question: Should OpenClaw define first-class WebChat prompt shortcuts, and if so should definitions be owned by WebChat state/config, command or skill metadata, or a plugin/Control UI contribution surface?
rationale: The code gap is real, but implementation requires choosing a new user-facing shortcut/storage/API contract and how it relates to existing command discovery and plugin UI direction.

options.title: Extend command or skill metadata first
options.body: Use the existing commands.list, skill, or plugin-command path as the discoverability source and add prompt-snippet semantics only if maintainers want that as a public contract.

options.title: Create WebChat-owned shortcuts
options.body: Add a dedicated WebChat shortcut store and sidebar, accepting the new config or persisted-state surface and migration/docs work that comes with it.

options.title: Defer to plugin UI panels
options.body: Keep this issue open as a consumer of the broader Control UI contribution-slot work rather than adding a core-only shortcut panel now.

recommendation.title: Extend command or skill metadata first
recommendation.body: Use the existing commands.list, skill, or plugin-command path as the discoverability source and add prompt-snippet semantics only if maintainers want that as a public contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is product/API direction across Control UI, config, and plugin boundaries, and steipete is a recent current-main contributor in the relevant chat UI area.
